lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Body Signals and Fueling My Day
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: sleep and rest as fuel

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy Ready for Life elementary sequence — Grade 3
Ready for Life v1 safety, supervision, and no-shame policy reference
Manuel Academy RFL G3 Unit 4 — body signals, rest, and food variety
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice sleep and rest as fuel. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: On a regular night, the learner walks through their own household's bedtime routine with a guardian nearby, naming each step out loud as it happens, and the next morning describes how rested their body felt without comparing to a number of hours or to anyone else's schedule.
safetyNotes: This is not a numeric or comparative sleep score; no specific number of hours is required or recorded.
Bedtime routines look different in every household; there is no single correct routine or wake-up time.
If a night's schedule does not allow the routine to be observed, use the written or drawn reflection alternative instead.

simulationAlternative.description: If the routine cannot be observed on a given night, the learner instead writes or draws a description of a typical bedtime routine from memory, naming the same three steps and the same rest signal, for equal credit.

materials: learner-local: paper and a pencil for notes

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Think about one step in your bedtime routine that seemed to help your body settle down the most. Describe that step and why you think it helped.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Routine awareness: The learner names three specific steps of the routine in order. | Signal recognition: The learner names one specific body signal that indicated readiness for rest, such as heavy eyelids, yawning, or stillness. | Morning connection: The learner names one specific way their body felt rested the next morning, without stating a number of hours. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner run the same routine on a second night and compare, in writing, whether the same rest signal showed up at the same step both nights.

resources.title: sleep and rest as fuel coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: On a regular night, the learner walks through their own household's bedtime routine with a guardian nearby, naming each step out loud as it happens, and the next morning describes how rested their body felt without comparing to a number of hours or to anyone else's schedule.
Coach direction: Before bedtime, think about what you already do most nights.
Learner prompt: Name one step you already do most nights before sleeping, such as brushing teeth, reading, or turning off lights.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: sleep and rest as fuel complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Walk through your bedtime routine tonight, naming each step out loud as you do it, with your guardian nearby to confirm.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named each step of my bedtime routine out loud as I did it.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I named one signal that told me my body was ready for rest, such as heavy eyelids, yawning, or feeling still.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I did not compare my bedtime or wake-up time to anyone else's schedule.
Response 4 (t2-p4): My guardian confirmed the routine happened.

Equal-access rule: If the routine cannot be observed on a given night, the learner instead writes or draws a description of a typical bedtime routine from memory, naming the same three steps and the same rest signal, for equal credit.

resources.title: sleep and rest as fuel minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Think about one step in your bedtime routine that seemed to help your body settle down the most. Describe that step and why you think it helped.

Success checks: Routine awareness: The learner names three specific steps of the routine in order. | Signal recognition: The learner names one specific body signal that indicated readiness for rest, such as heavy eyelids, yawning, or stillness. | Morning connection: The learner names one specific way their body felt rested the next morning, without stating a number of hours.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: sleep and rest as fuel supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional sleep and rest as fuel condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Routine awareness: The learner names three specific steps of the routine in order. | Signal recognition: The learner names one specific body signal that indicated readiness for rest, such as heavy eyelids, yawning, or stillness. | Morning connection: The learner names one specific way their body felt rested the next morning, without stating a number of hours..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g3-u04-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
